We need to propose a 3-step retrosynthesis for target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have hints: step1 forward: carboxylic acid to amide (coupling). So retrosynthesis: break amide bond to give carboxylic acid and amine.

Step2 forward: Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (the double bond). So retrosynthesis: break the C=C double bond and carboxylic acid to give aromatic aldehyde and malonic acid? Actually Doebner gives unsaturated acid from aldehyde + malonic acid. So reverse: from unsaturated acid, we can get aldehyde + malonic acid.

Our target contains /C=C/C(=O)N... So the unsaturated acid part is the side chain attached to aromatic sulfonyl phenyl: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. The unsaturated acid is actually an α,β-unsaturated amide? Wait: /C=C/C(=O)N... The carbonyl is amide, not acid. But Doebner modification forms unsaturated carboxylic acid, not amide. However we could have first Doebner to give unsaturated acid, then convert acid to amide (step1). So retrosynthesis: target -> break amide to give unsaturated acid (C=O N) -> then break unsaturated acid to aldehyde + malonic acid (or maybe malonic acid derivative). Then step3: sulfonamide formation: sulfonyl chloride + amine to give sulfonamide. In target, we have NS(=O)(=O) attached to aromatic ring. So retrosynthesis: break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonyl fluoride) and aniline. So we need three steps: 1) amide formation (coupling) 2) Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid) 3) sulfonamide formation (sulfonyl chloride + aniline). That matches hints.

Thus we need to propose precursors:

Target: A: aromatic ring with methyl (p-tolyl) attached to sulfonamide linking to second aromatic ring (phenyl sulfone). So we can split at sulfonamide: precursor1: p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(N)cc1) and sulfonyl chloride: ClSO2-c2ccc(... )? Actually sulfonyl chloride attached to second aromatic ring bearing the side chain (unsaturated amide). So sulfonyl chloride: ClSO2-c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2.

Then step2: that sulfonyl chloride precursor contains unsaturated amide side chain. We break amide to give unsaturated acid: /C=C/C(=O)N... -> unsaturated acid: /C=C/COOH attached to aromatic ring. So precursor2: ClSO2-c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2.

Step3: that unsaturated acid derived from Doebner: break double bond and acid to give aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). So precursor3: aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) and malonic acid.

Thus overall route: final target from p-toluidine + sulfonyl chloride (step3). Sulfonyl chloride from unsaturated acid via amide formation? Wait order: forward steps: 1) sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride) -> product sulfonamide (intermediate). 2) Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid) -> unsaturated acid (intermediate). 3) amide coupling (acid + amine) -> final target. So retrosynthesis order reversed: target -> break amide -> unsaturated acid + aniline (actually the amine is the aniline attached to sulfonyl? Wait amide coupling involves the amine that is part of the side chain: Nc3ccccc3N is an aniline attached to amide carbonyl. The amide nitrogen is attached to aromatic amine (aniline). So breaking amide gives unsaturated acid (attached to sulfonyl phenyl) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So step1 retrosynthesis: target -> unsaturated acid (aryl with side chain) + aniline.

Step2: unsaturated acid -> aromatic aldehyde (aryl) + malonic acid (via Doebner reverse). The aromatic aldehyde is the same phenyl ring (c2ccc(CHO)cc2). So step2 gives aldehyde + malonic acid.

Step3: sulfonamide formation: combine p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(N)cc1) with sulfonyl chloride derived from aldehyde? Actually sulfonyl chloride is attached to the aromatic ring that had aldehyde. So after step2 we have aldehyde aromatic ring; we need to convert that aldehyde to sulfonyl chloride? Wait sulfonyl chloride is attached to the aromatic ring via SO2Cl group. The sulfonyl chloride is derived from the same aromatic ring (c2ccc(SO2Cl)cc2). So we need to form sulfonyl chloride from the aldehyde? Not typical. Actually sulfonyl chloride is usually from sulfonation of aromatic ring then chlorination. But in retrosynthesis we can consider sulfonyl chloride as a commercial building block. So step3: combine p-toluidine with sulfonyl chloride (c2ccc(SO2Cl)cc2) to give sulfonamide intermediate (which still has unsaturated acid side chain? Wait sulfonyl chloride must already have the side chain attached (unsaturated acid). So the sulfonyl chloride is c2ccc(SO2Cl) with side chain? Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the aromatic ring that also bears the side chain. So the sulfonyl chloride is: ClSO2-c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2. So step3: sulfonamide formation between p-toluidine and that sulfonyl chloride gives sulfonamide intermediate (still with unsaturated acid). Then step2 amide coupling? Wait order: The amide coupling is between unsaturated acid and aniline (c3ccccc3N). That amine is not the same as p-toluidine. So after sulfonamide formation we have sulfonamide intermediate with unsaturated acid attached. Then amide coupling attaches the aniline to the acid, giving final target. So forward order: 1) sulfonamide formation (p-toluidine + sulfonyl chloride) -> sulfonamide intermediate (aryl-sulfonyl-aryl with unsaturated acid). 2) amide coupling (unsaturated acid + aniline) -> final target. But the hint order enumerated: carboxylic acid to amide, Doebner modification, sulfonamide formation. That suggests forward steps: first amide formation, then Doebner, then sulfonamide. But we can propose any order as long as three steps.

Let's follow hint order: Step1 forward: amide formation (acid + amine). So starting materials: unsaturated acid (aryl with side chain) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). That gives intermediate: aryl-sulfonyl-aryl with amide (but still lacking sulfonamide). Step2 forward: Doebner modification to create unsaturated acid from aldehyde + malonic acid. So the unsaturated acid precursor is formed from aldehyde (aryl-CHO) + malonic acid. Step3 forward: sulfonamide formation between p-toluidine and sulfonyl chloride (aryl-SO2Cl). The sulfonyl chloride must be derived from the aldehyde? Actually after Doebner we have unsaturated acid attached to aromatic ring, not sulfonyl chloride. So we need sulfonyl chloride as separate building block: p-toluidine + sulfonyl chloride (aryl-SO2Cl) -> sulfonamide intermediate (aryl-SO2-NH-p-tolyl) with unsaturated acid side chain? Wait the sulfonyl chloride must have the unsaturated acid side chain attached to the aromatic ring. So we need to generate that sulfonyl chloride from the aldehyde? Not typical. But we can treat sulfonyl chloride as a commercial reagent that already has the side chain (i.e., ClSO2-c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2). So step3 forward: combine p-toluidine with that sulfonyl chloride to give sulfonamide intermediate (still with unsaturated acid). Then step1 amide coupling attaches aniline to the acid to give final product. The Doebner step is used to synthesize the sulfonyl chloride precursor from aldehyde + malonic acid, then chlorination? But we can ignore chlorination.

Simplify: Provide retrosynthetic route:

1) Break amide: target -> intermediate A (sulfonamide with unsaturated acid) + aniline (c3ccccc3N).

2) Break sulfonamide: intermediate A -> p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(N)cc1) + sulfonyl chloride bearing unsaturated acid (ClSO2-c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2).

3) Break unsaturated acid via Doebner: sulfonyl chloride precursor -> aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) + malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). (Assume chlorination later.)

Thus three reactions: amide coupling, sulfonamide formation, Doebner modification.

Now we need to produce JSON route with type mol root target, children reaction nodes.

We need template IDs for each reaction. We have template 401931 for amide formation (looks like amide formation from acid and amine with double bond). That template matches pattern: amide formation from acid and alkene? Actually template 401931 is amide formation from acid and amine with double bond? The SMARTS shows [#7:2]-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:3])/[CH;D2;+0:4]=[C:5]>>... So forward reaction is amide formation from acid? It seems to be amide formation from acid and amine with double bond? The product side is amide with C=C? Actually the product side is amide with double bond? The template seems to convert an amide with C=C to something else. But we can assume it's suitable for amide coupling.

We need template for sulfonamide formation. Search.
